name: James
overview: James was a male fisherman and one of the Twelve apostles of YHVH, uniquely identified as the son of Zebedee. He was involved in mending nets before being called to discipleship, highlighting his humble origins and direct call to follow Jesus. His role as one of the Twelve underscores his close association with Jesus' earthly ministry.
namesAndTitles: The proper name 'James' means 'follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel,' indicating a sense of following or succession. He was also given the title 'Son of thunder,' a divine designation referring to a noisy or forceful nature, which reveals a distinctive aspect of his character as recognized by Jesus.
familyAndRelationships: James was the explicit son of Zebedee and had a brother named John, inferred from their shared parentage. Both brothers were called from their fishing occupation to become disciples and apostles of YHVH, indicating a family deeply involved in Jesus' mission.
scriptureSignificance: James holds significance as a devoted follower of Jesus who transitioned from a fisherman to an apostle, demonstrating the transformative power of Christ's call. His inclusion among the Twelve and his familial ties to John highlight his integral role in the early church. His life exemplifies the necessity of personal faith and active discipleship within the Christian narrative.

keyEvents.event: Did not believe in Jesus initially
Jesus appeared to him after resurrection
